purpose: Isosorbide mononitrate is used to prevent chest pain (angina) in people with heart disease. It does not stop chest pain that has already started, but it helps keep angina attacks from happening in the first place. It is often used by people who have coronary artery disease to help them stay active with less discomfort.
how_it_works: This medication works by relaxing and widening your blood vessels, especially the veins. When your veins are wider, less blood returns to your heart at one time, which means your heart does not have to work as hard. This reduces the oxygen demand on your heart and helps prevent chest pain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a headache, especially when you first start taking it — this usually gets better after a few weeks. You may also feel dizzy, lightheaded, or flushed, especially when you stand up quickly. Nausea and low blood pressure are also possible.
warnings: Never stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger chest pain. Do not take erectile dysfunction medications like Viagra, Cialis, or Levitra while on this drug — the combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines you take. If you feel dizzy, sit or lie down slowly to avoid falling.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 30 mg to 60 mg once daily in the morning for the extended-release tablet (Imdur). Your doctor may increase your dose to 120 mg once daily if needed. It is important to take it at the same time each day and to leave a nitrate-free period of about 8 hours (usually overnight) to prevent your body from becoming resistant to the medication.
